desc:
Look at every contiguous block of exactly k elements of nums in which all values are different. Return the largest sum among those blocks, or 0 if no block qualifies.

nums = [4, 2, 4, 5, 6, 2], k = 3
blocks: [4,2,4] x   [2,4,5] 11   [4,5,6] 15   [5,6,2] 13
result = 15
hints: A window is valid only if it contains no repeated value. How can you know that without rebuilding a set each time?
Keep a frequency map and the number of distinct keys. The window has all distinct values exactly when the distinct count equals k.
Maintain the window sum alongside the map. After each slide, if distinct == k, the current sum is a candidate for the answer.
editorial: Maintain three things for the current window: the sum, a frequency map and the number of distinct values. Sliding adds one element and removes one, each in O(1).

Because the window has exactly k elements, it holds k distinct values if and only if it contains no duplicate. After every slide (including the first window) check distinct == k and update the best sum. The answer starts at 0, which also covers the no-valid-window case. Time O(n), space O(k).
